page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sucker of Chrysanthemum
lines: Sucker: a lateral branch from the underground
part of the stem; it grows horizontally
beneath the soil and then comes out obliquely
steps.why: The sucker's identity is its path: it STARTS underground and SURFACES upward. Both halves of the path must be written.
common_mistakes: Calling the sucker a root. It is a stem branch - it carries buds and gives a new shoot.
steps.memory_tip: Sucker surfaces: born under the soil, comes up into the air.
steps.margin_note: Write the path - underground, horizontal, then obliquely up.

steps.label: Stolon of jasmine

lines.text: Stolon: a slender AERIAL lateral branch from

lines: the base of the main stem.
It grows up for some time, bends down to
touch the ground and produces adventitious
steps.why: The stolon runs the opposite path to the sucker: it starts in the air and bends down to the ground. The contrast of paths is the whole difference.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two paths. Sucker: soil to air. Stolon: air to soil.
steps.memory_tip: Sucker goes up and out of the soil; stolon stoops down into it.
steps.margin_note: The words aerial and bends down are the scoring contrast.
